label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8) whose first two tokens avoid a suppressing set
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, about to output original token 0); never in the original or copy phases. Strongly length-dependent: there is essentially no firing for L<=6, and the rate at <DEL> is 1.3% for L=7, 5.7% for L=8 and 8.3% for L=9 (raw counts; 62% of mass is at L=9). Within long sequences it is gated by the identity of the first original tokens (the one about to be output) in a graded, roughly additive way. First tokens c,h,i,k,l,n,o,r,v,2 give 55-82% firing; b,e,g,q,s,t,y,z,0 give ~0%; f,j,m,p,u,w,3 are intermediate. The second token follows the same pattern: b,e,g,q,s,t,y,z,0 (and f) suppress, and c,d,h,i,k,l,n,o,r,v give >90% firing when the first token is favorable. The third token has a weaker effect. The highest activations are L=9 sequences starting with i/o/2/v followed by a favorable token (e.g. k). Predicate: test F1 ~0.74; misses are mostly L=7 cases and borderline tokens, so the true rule looks like a soft threshold on length plus a per-token score of the first few tokens, not a clean boolean.
